cohort: Pregnant women in their second trimester, either with isolated gestational proteinuria (>=300 mg/24-hour) or without proteinuria/hypertension, were followed at a tertiary center.
finding: Isolated gestational proteinuria (IGP) was associated with a 12-fold increased risk of developing preeclampsia, but unless hypertension developed, maternal and neonatal outcomes were similar to healthy pregnant women.
mod_finding: Delivery mode was measured as an outcome and found to be similar between the isolated gestational proteinuria and control groups.
